Acaulon integrifolium Pottiaceae                                             WSTVAN
The shoots ofthis species form open colonies on bare soil, never more
than about2 mm or so tall. The green to brown, ovate leaves are slightly
U-s)laped in cross-section, with a pointed apex and entire margins.
The·cost� reaches the apex, occasionally being slightly excurrent. The
distinctive orange, globular capsule is topped by a minute apiculus,
and is held on a short seta.

Aloina aloides var. ambigua Pottiaceae                                          WSVN
In dry calcareous country this minute species is very common on soil,
especially on roadsides, very-obvious when there are capsules but
otherwise rather cryptic. The shoots are only about 2 mm tall, the leaves
spr�ading from a short stem when moist but ·strongly incurved when
dry. The green, oblong leaves (to 3 x 0.7 mm) are thick and slightly
concave, with the margins inflexed and the apex distinctly hooded.
There is a costa but it is not obvious because ofthe thickness ofthe leaf.
In the upper part ofthe leafit is covered by minute filaments. The dark
brown capsule, 3 to 3.5 mm long, is more or less cylindrical, with a
long-beaked operculum, on a seta 15-20 mm long.
    A. sullivaniana (WSVN) is a si�ilar species, but the leaf ends in a long, hyaline
hairpoint. A. rigida (S) is also very similar, and possibly introduced from Europe. It is
distinguished microscopically by 1 to 3 rows of long, narrow cells at the basal
margins.
    Crossidium geheebii (WSVN) has a distinct costa and recurved (not inrolled)
margins, and the capsule is only 1 or 2 mm long. C. davidai (WSV) has
spathulate leaves with a distinctly pointed apex, and the margins are incurved
slightly near the apex.

WIKIPEDIA  (1) 
Aloina is a genus of mosses belonging to the family Pottiaceae first described by Nils Conrad Kindberg. It has a cosmopolitan distribution.
